A vertical inertia force acts along the centre of the attachment pattern, so it divides equally between the four fittings and produces no couple. A horizontal force acts below the attachment plane: it adds a couple that the fore and aft pairs resist with a pair of vertical reactions, which is what the couple share column carries.

The manoeuvre case governs, not the emergency landing: the factor of safety of 27.303 lifts 3.5 g of limit manoeuvre to 5.25 g of ultimate load, which is more than the 3.0 g the platform declares for the emergency landing. The strength checks are not what sizes this installation: the declared capability of the platform provision is 25 kN per point and the largest reaction is under 1 kN.

## Hand calculation against the general solution

The case with the largest couple is LC-EML-FWD. A hand calculation takes the direct share and the couple share:

- even share of the inertia force between the four fittings: `peak reaction per fitting = F / number of fittings`
- couple from the inertia force acting below the attachment plane: `added reaction per fitting = F * e / (2 * pair spacing)`

| Component | Closed form (N) | General solution (N) | Difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Direct share | 581.3 | 581.3 | 0.00 % |
| Couple share | 148.6 | 148.6 | 0.00 % |

The two methods agree on both components to within 0.00 %, which is what the check verifies. They do not agree on the total, and that is the part worth investigating: the closed form adds the two shares and gets 730 N, the general solution resolves them as a vector and gets 600 N, **+21.6 %**. The shares act on different axes, so adding them is not a conservative simplification but a different quantity; here it overestimates the fitting load, which is the safe direction for a hand calculation but would be the wrong number to publish. The check on the fitting uses the resultant.

## Deflection

Under LC-MAN-UP at limit load the payload moves 2.18 mm relative to the platform, with the load path stiffness of 933 N/mm and the softest support idealisation, which gives the largest movement. The installation has 5.0 mm available at its tightest field of view direction (30.0 mm measured against the required clearance), so the movement stays inside it.

## Resonance

| Rotor | Harmonic | Band (Hz) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 1/rev | 5.25 to 7.33 |
| main | 2/rev | 10.50 to 14.67 |
| main | 3/rev | 15.75 to 22.00 |
| tail | 1/rev | 30.00 to 44.00 |
| tail | 2/rev | 60.00 to 88.00 |

Admissible windows: 0.00 to 5.25 Hz, 7.33 to 10.50 Hz, 14.67 to 15.75 Hz, 22.00 to 30.00 Hz, 44.00 to 60.00 Hz, 88.00 to 200.00 Hz.

The installation is estimated at **21.9 to 43.3 Hz** for a modal mass of 49.4 kg, between the simply supported and the clamped idealisation of the frame rails.

**The separation is not demonstrated.** The estimate lands inside the bands, and no window is wide enough to contain the interval between the two idealisations: the uncertainty of the estimate is larger than the distance between the harmonics. Raising the first mode above the highest band would need 136 mm square rails of the declared wall thickness, **8.8 kg instead of 5.6 kg** of frame, which is +3.2 kg against a kit budget of 15 kg that has 1.40 kg left. The installation therefore needs a modal analysis or a ground vibration test on the first article, and possibly a damper, rather than a stiffer frame (OI-02).

## Open items

- **OI-01 — Emergency landing factors are platform data, not a clause of CS-27 for this installation** The declared factors (3.0 g up, 3.0 g down, 4.0 g forward, 4.0 g aft, 2.0 g lateral) are the platform structural criteria. 14 CFR 27.561(b) gives ultimate factors of 4 g up, 16 g forward, 8 g sideward, 20 g down and 1.5 g rearward, but it applies to each occupant and to items of mass inside the cabin; this payload is mounted outside the cabin, so the clause does not cover it directly. 27.561(c) applies to items of mass above and behind the cabin and 27.561(d) to structure in the fuel tank area, which are also not this installation. The load cases therefore run on declared platform data, treated as ultimate, and the traceability of those factors has to be confirmed by the platform before the requirement is closed.
- **OI-02 — The resonance separation is not demonstrated** The single degree of freedom estimate of the installation's first natural frequency, over the declared support idealisations, lands inside the main rotor 2/rev and 3/rev excitation bands and inside the tail rotor 1/rev band, and no admissible window between the bands is wide enough to contain it. The stiffness of the real installation, its damping and the platform impedance have to come from a modal analysis or from a ground vibration test on the first article; a stiffness increase big enough to clear the bands costs more frame mass than the 15 kg budget of SYS005 can take (see the report).
- **OI-03 — Plate, weld and fastener-slip flexibility** The interface plate, the welded frame joints and the slip of the bolted joints are not modelled: the compliance of the load path is taken as the frame rails in series with the fitting brackets. A finite element model of the assembly would be needed to include them, and a test to confirm.

## What this evidence does not cover

- The payload mounting interface and the interface plate are not checked: they belong to the payload supplier and to a plate bending model this study does not have (OI-03).
- The welded joints of the frame are not sized: a weld schedule and its allowables are not declared (OI-03).
- The loads are quasi-static. No fatigue spectrum, no dynamic amplification and no rotor-induced vibratory load is applied.
- The material allowables are declared handbook values, not certified values (A-014).
